Research

What we work on.

Our research spans the full arc of the dark matter problem — from the underlying particle theory, through the experiments that could detect it, to the instrumentation and analysis techniques that make those experiments possible. Six interconnected themes structure the group's work.

Themes Publications Presentations Achievements

Themes

Direct dark matter phenomenology

Non-relativistic effective field theory through to UV-complete mediator models — bridging fundamental physics and detector observables across argon, xenon, germanium and beyond.

Explore →

DarkSide experiment

Contributions to DarkSide-20k at Gran Sasso and reinterpretation of DarkSide-50 data across spin-independent, spin-dependent and effective-field-theory motivated dark matter models.

Explore →

Instrumentation development

Detector and readout technology development for next-generation rare-event searches.

Explore →

Opto-mechanical levitating sensors

Optically and magnetically levitated mesoscopic sensors as a route to ultra-low-threshold detection — sensitivity projections, signal modelling and physics-case studies for a new class of experiment.

Explore →

Neutrinos

CEvNS in dual-target direct-detection experiments, beyond-Standard-Model neutrino physics, and Xe-136 neutrinoless double beta decay — with connections to colliders, levitating sensors and phenomenology.

Explore →

Collider physics

ATLAS at the LHC — connecting past and future interests in dark-sector and beyond-Standard-Model searches at high-energy colliders.

Explore →
